note: Rewritten from Miller 1943; original in English; the OCR is clear, and the measurements keep the original's specimen-by-specimen lists (the original table gives no range). The original name is Kalotermes (Calcaritermes) nearcticus Snyder; the soldier and nymph are described here for the first time.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head semicylindrical, truncate anteriorly, the dorsal line slightly concave in side view; frontal surface with a single deep longitudinal groove, shallowest above the labrum and deepest on the frons. Sides of the head parallel in dorsal view. Head colour black anteriorly, becoming more or less abruptly paler reddish brown behind the level of the antennae, then brownish yellow further back (in some specimens the whole head is paler). Frontal surface slightly rough, the whole head finely punctate. Mandibles reddish brown to black, slightly reduced, in side view less than half the head length; right mandible with 2 teeth, left with 3. Labrum and antennae yellow. Antennae 10 or 11-segmented, the segments nearly equal in size except the basal segment. Weak lamellar projections from the head lie above and below the antennal socket. Compound eyes extremely reduced, about 0.1 mm in diameter, pale; situated slightly above the antennal base, their distance from the antennal base twice their own diameter. Anterior part of the pronotum concave and smooth, the sides convexly and smoothly narrowing towards the posterior margin; the width at the anterior margin about 2.5 times the median length of the pronotum. Tip of the fore tibia with a distinct, basally broad spine on the outer margin. Postmentum brown to dark brown, yellowish anteriorly, the margins generally darker, wider in the middle. Measurements (mm, 5 soldiers of the Winter Park series, morphotype first): head width at the posterior margin 1.2, 1.2, 1.2, 1.15, 1.15; head width at the level of the antennae 1.15, 1.1, 1.1, 1.05, 1.05; head length to the tip of the labrum 1.55, 1.75, 1.5, 1.4, 1.45; head length to the frontal groove 1.1, 1.1, 1.15, 1.0, 1.1; head depth (dorsoventral, in side view) 1.05, 1.0, 1.0, 1.0, 0.95; left mandible length (tip to condyle) 0.64, 0.67, 0.62, 0.62; pronotum width 1.25, 1.25, 1.2, 1.1, 1.2; pronotum median length 0.45, 0.5, 0.5, 0.4, 0.4; pronotum length at the margin 0.70, 0.65, 0.70, 0.55, 0.55; number of antennal segments 10, 11, 11, 11, broken.

sections.label: Nymph
sections.text: The nymph shows no marked peculiarity other than a slightly raised area in the middle of the mesonotum, bearing numerous reddish rough points. Snyder had recorded a similar feature in Calcaritermes emarginicollis, and at his suggestion it was observed in the nymph of C. nearcticus.

sections.label: Other
sections.text: The description is based on 15 soldiers from Florida: Orlando (11 miles north of Winter Park), 12 September 1940 (month 9, day 12), collected by E. M. Miller (the morphotype series); Bartow, 24 November 1940 (month 11, day 24), E. M. Miller; Ortega, 17 March 1941 (month 3, day 17), A. E. Emerson; Ortega, 17 March 1941 (month 3, day 17), Victor Dropkin. The paper also records one intermediate individual with wing pads and a tibial spine. The alate is identified from the description of Snyder (1933); the specimens used are in the U.S. National Museum (No. 161193) and elsewhere.
